messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Participants in the lowest 25(OH)D quartile were more likely to report depressive symptoms than those in the highest quartile.
Sentence: "When investigating the relationship between the presence versus absence of depressive symptoms and quartiles of 25(OH)D, participants in the lowest quartile were more likely to report depressive symptoms compared with those in the highest quartile."
Measured as: presence of depressive symptoms (CES-D)
Population: 615 non-clinical young adults in Dunedin, New Zealand
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D quartile (measured, not given)
Comparator: Highest 25(OH)D quartile
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 615
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational vitamin D level studies on depression, but Study A (healthy young adults, cross-sectional, CES-D symptoms) and Study B (post-COVID inpatients, cohort, PHQ-9 >5 at six months) differ mainly in who was enrolled, so their opposing directions likely reflect population.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: non-clinical young adults in New Zealand vs older hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Spain; Study B's direction is not stated in the abstract"}
